summary: streak-metrics-math ships and executes a RedShell C2 backdoor on import
details: The package advertises itself as a streak/calendar math helper with a 'native math accelerator', but its main entry contains a top-level IIFE that resolves the shipped ELF at dist/math-calc.bin, chmods it 0o755, and spawns it detached whenever a consumer requires or imports the module. A SHA-256 comparison against a hardcoded expected hash is present but inverted (mismatch is logged as 'Using cached native accelerator', match as 'verified'), and the binary is executed unconditionally. The bundled ELF is a RedShell C2 implant: it connects over TLS to the hardcoded IP 217.60.77.63, sends a SECURE_BEACON identification string, and accepts remote commands that pipe attacker-supplied input to /bin/sh and /bin/bash on the installer's host. The implant additionally fetches secondary ELFs/shellcode from http://<C2>/Others/<name> and /SC/<name>, chmods and runs them, and supports memfd_create-based fileless execution via a python3 syscall(319) helper. Operator commands /ssh_keys, /creds, /dbfind, /download, and /dataextract collect SSH keys, credentials, and arbitrary files and stream them to the C2 via chunked HTTP POST to /api/extract-receive. A /redshell persist command writes a user systemd unit ~/.config/systemd/user/svc-update.service pointing at /proc/self/exe and enables it for reboot persistence.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
